Ever tried stepping through a PL/pgSQL routine and felt stuck?
Now dbForge 2026.2 brings a built‑in PostgreSQL debugger that lets you set breakpoints,
watch variables,
and step line by line.
It feels like debugging any other code,
but right inside your database client.

I started using the new visual object editors yesterday.
Drag‑and‑drop columns,
rename tables,
or adjust constraints without writing a single ALTER statement.
The UI updates the underlying DDL instantly,
which saves a lot of copy‑paste work.

The AI assistant also got smarter.
It now understands the broader context of your schema,
so when you ask it to generate a query it can reference related tables automatically.

Here are a few ways this can help you right now:

- Faster issue isolation with the debugger,
reducing time spent on trial‑and‑error.
- Visual editors cut down manual script errors,
especially for quick schema tweaks.
- AI‑enhanced suggestions keep you from forgetting joins or column names.

Have you tried the new debugger yet,
and how does it change your workflow?

#PostgreSQL #DatabaseTools #DataEngineering #dbForge

concept_posts.post_content:
Ever found yourself debugging a downstream job because the source data suddenly changed shape?

I’ve been there too,
 and it usually comes down to missing data contracts.

A data contract is basically a written agreement between the producer and consumer of data.
Think of it like a simple API spec that says,
 “I will deliver a JSON payload with fields id (int),
 name (string),
 and event_ts (ISO timestamp) every hour.”

When we treat that contract like code – version it,
 test it,
 and publish it – downstream pipelines can trust the shape and focus on transformation instead of firefighting.

Key takeaways:
- Define the schema,
 data quality rules,
 and delivery cadence up front.
- Version contracts and deprecate old fields with a clear migration window.
- Automate contract validation as part of CI/CD pipelines.

A common mistake is to treat contracts as optional documentation and rely on informal emails.
That leads to silent breaking changes.

How do you currently manage data contracts in your projects?

#DataEngineering #DataContracts #APIDesign #DataOps
